Complete match rules and guidance for the main Dominó PE surfaces.
The match is played by 4 players in 2 partnerships, with partners seated opposite each other. The first team to reach 6 points or more wins the match.

The game uses a 28-tile double-six set. Each player receives 6 tiles. The 4 remaining tiles are sleepers: they stay out of play and are never drawn. A double is a tile with the same value on both halves, such as 6–6 or 3–3.

The first play of a round is the opening play. In the first round, and after a tied pip count between opposing teams, the starting player is the one holding the highest available double, in this mandatory order: 6–6, 5–5, 4–4, 3–3, 2–2. That double must be the opening tile. Because there are 5 candidate doubles and only 4 sleepers, at least one of them is always in play.
After a round with one individual winner, that player starts the next round and may lead any tile. If both partners on the winning team tie for the lowest pip count, the next starting player is chosen at random between them with a 50/50 chance, and may also lead any tile.
Turns move counterclockwise. On each turn, play one tile whose value matches one of the open ends. If the current player has no playable tile, the turn passes automatically to the next player.

A finish happens when a player plays the last tile in hand, winning the round for the partnership.
• Standard finish — 1 point: a non-double tile that can be played on only one open end. • Double finish — 2 points: a double that can be played on only one open end. • Two-way finish — 3 points: a non-double tile that could be played on either open end. • Two-way double finish — 4 points: a double that could be played on either open end.
Blocked round, pip count and ties

A round is blocked when no player has a playable tile. Each player totals the pips remaining in hand; the team containing the player with the lowest individual pip count wins. A pip-count win is worth 1 point.
If the 2 players tied for the lowest count are partners, their team wins normally and the next starting player is chosen 50/50 between them. If the lowest count is tied between opposing teams, nobody scores and the next round is worth 2×. If another such tie occurs, the following round is worth 3×, then 4×, and so on until there is a winner. The multiplier applies to the value of the finish that wins that round.
Matches with a clock show the available time next to the player. Make your move before time runs out; the interface indicates when an automatic action is required.
Public ranked matches require a connected account. Private rooms and local matches follow the options shown in the play menu and do not enter the public leaderboard.
The public leaderboard shows current and closed cycles. Standings and details shown on screen are updated as eligible results are recorded by the service.
